sections.h2: Selling a house in De Pere
sections.html: About five miles south of Green Bay on the Fox River, De Pere (Brown County) counted an estimated 25,590 residents in 2025. A sale runs through three offices: the city handles permits and assessment, the Brown County Register of Deeds takes the deed, and the Brown County Treasurer keeps tax records. Whether you list, sell yourself or take a cash offer from a buyer who accepts the house as is, the sections below explain what affects price and timing.

About a third of De Pere households rent, which makes tenants a regular part of local sales. Older, larger homes sit on streets near the river, including Broadway, Ridgeway Boulevard, Morris, Fulton and Franklin, and several of those blocks are in National Register historic districts. Newer subdivisions lie away from the water. The city is split between two school districts, so check yours before quoting schools to a buyer.

A riverfront seller should expect questions about the cleanup of PCB-contaminated sediment in the Lower Fox River below the De Pere dam, completed in 2020.

De Pere has revalued every property each year since 2018, which keeps assessments close to market. Accurate Appraisal, LLC of Menasha does the work under contract. The city notes that assessors do not set tax rates and that a revaluation leaves the city's total collection unchanged. In the 2024 update, its explainer reported an average rise of about 8 to 10 percent.

  • Open Book: a brief meeting with an assessor, in person or by phone, to go over your value.
  • Still unhappy? Appeal to the Board of Review, five residents appointed by the mayor.
  • The City Clerk, 339-4050, schedules the hearing, and you file a Formal Objection Application. The assessor's value is presumed correct until you prove otherwise with facts.

Call the Brown County Treasurer at (920) 448-4074 whenever a property's mailing address changes. After you sell, pass along the buyer's mailing address so the next bill lands with the right person, and have the title company show how this year's tax is divided at closing.

A buyer may ask the city for building records showing whether permits were pulled and the work passed, which makes permit history a bargaining point. Request the record for your parcel from the Building Department (920-339-4053, dpbldg@deperewi.gov) before you list.

  • A permit is needed for new construction, repairs, additions, alterations and demolitions, covering boilers, furnaces, wiring, plumbing fixtures, garages, porches, fences, decks, pools and sheds.
  • Beginning work with no permit doubles the fee and can bring a stop work order.
  • Building permits last one year, or two for a one- or two-family dwelling.
  • New windows and altered exits or light openings may need one too.

The city warns that work not finished to code can hurt insurability and a sale. Found something open? Finish it and close the permit before listing, and most buyers stop worrying. When zoning or code cannot be met, variance requests go to the Zoning Board of Appeals for a $175 fee.

The city also regulates short-term rentals. Listing a house on Airbnb, VRBO or a similar site takes a Tourist Rooming House license, obtained in two steps. Apply first to Development Services with a $100 fee. Once approved, the Health Department's sanitarian explains the license process, and no rental is allowed until the pre-inspection is done.

A house with a short-term rental history should have its license status confirmed with Development Services before listing, because a buyer planning the same use will ask.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Brown County
sections.html:
The office is in the Northern Building, Room 260, 305 E. Walnut Street, Green Bay (920-448-4470). It is open 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday to Thursday and 7:30 to 11:30 a.m. on Friday, and it takes walk-in real estate recordings until 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and until 10:30 a.m. Friday.

Tag-less recording is now standard. If you file on paper, you also submit a Swift Agreement and then get an email with a secure link good for up to three printed copies over seven days.

The deed needs a state transfer return as well. Wis. Stat. 77.22 puts the grantor on the hook for 30 cents per $100 of value, with the return filed electronically. The fee is noted on the face of the deed, and an exempt sale must state its reason there.

sections.h2: What a De Pere seller must disclose
sections.html:
Chapter 709 reaches sales, exchanges and land contracts for one to four dwelling units and for vacant land, but not dwellings never lived in. Owners fill out the state's condition report and deliver it within 10 days of contract acceptance.

If the report is late, the buyer gets a short window to cancel. Heirs selling an estate house are often covered by the exception for personal representatives, trustees and conservators who never lived there. Other sellers should answer every item, since a partly filled report is incomplete.

sections.h2: From contract to closing in De Pere
sections.html:
A sale in De Pere moves through the same handful of stops, and it helps to line them up early.

  1. Ask the Building Department for the parcel record and close any open permits.
  2. Check the license status of any short-term rental use with Development Services.
  3. Confirm your school district and share it accurately with buyers.
  4. Complete the condition report and deliver it within 10 days after the contract is accepted.
  5. Get a tax balance from the Brown County Treasurer and a net sheet from the title company.
  6. File the electronic transfer return, then record the deed in Green Bay.

If an assessor letter or Open Book question arrives while the house is under contract, call the assessor and keep the buyer informed, since open book is a quick and informal way to settle a value question. After closing, tell the treasurer the new mailing address so bills reach the right owner.

Listing works for a house that shows well and a seller who can wait for a buyer's loan. A cash sale works for open permits, deferred maintenance, tenants or an estate to close out.

Ask for a net sheet either way, covering the loan payoff, the transfer fee, recording, prorated taxes and repair credits, so you compare what you would actually receive. Add the Brown County Treasurer's tax balance and any open permit items to that sheet, and settle them before the closing date.

faqs.q: Who assesses property in De Pere?
faqs.a: Accurate Appraisal, LLC of Menasha, under contract with the city. De Pere has assessed every property annually since 2018, and owners can attend an Open Book session to discuss a value.

faqs.q: Where is a De Pere deed recorded?
faqs.a: The Brown County Register of Deeds in Green Bay, 920-448-4470, which requires a Swift Agreement with paper filings.

faqs.q: What is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a De Pere sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays 30 cents per $100 of value, and the return is filed electronically.

faqs.q: Can I rent my De Pere house on Airbnb before I sell?
faqs.a: Only under a Tourist Rooming House license, which needs a $100 application to Development Services and a Health Department sanitarian's pre-inspection first.

faqs.q: Does unpermitted work stop a De Pere sale?
faqs.a: It can surface in negotiation because buyers may request the city's building records. A permit started late costs double, so closing permits before listing usually costs less.
